stem: A GP is reviewing weight status in a 5-year-old; which is the standard tool for assessing unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years?
explanation: Body mass index (BMI) is the standard tool for assessing unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years. Interpretation should be based on age and growth stage.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: BMI is the standard tool for unhealthy weight assessment in children over 2 years, and it must be interpreted in the context of age and growth stage.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because mid-parental height charts are used to assess growth potential, not unhealthy weight.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because BMI is the standard tool for assessing unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because head circumference is used to assess head growth in infants and young children, not unhealthy weight.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because weight-for-age alone does not account for height and is not the standard tool for unhealthy weight assessment in this age group.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because bone age radiographs assess skeletal maturation, not unhealthy weight.
